business_summary.text: Sangam (India) Limited is a fully integrated textile maker producing PV and cotton yarn, denim and synthetic fabric, and seamless garments, with 6 plants in Rajasthan and exports to 50+ countries.

call_points.text: Any new capex benefits will not flow in FY27; planning will take about a quarter.
Management said there were no one-time inventory gains in Q4; margin improvement came from utilisation and efficiency.
Net debt to equity is about 1.1x; working capital cycle improved from 80 to 55 days.
call_points.versus_prior: reiterated working capital improvement from 80 to 55 days

call_points.text: Crude price volatility makes Q1 margin outlook uncertain; management said it can pass on a significant portion of costs.
C9 brand contributes 40-45% of garment business; balance is contract manufacturing.
FY26 revenue grew 12.9% to ₹3,243 Cr on volume expansion and demand across domestic and global markets.
FY26 gross margin was 40.1%, with management citing cost optimisation, operational efficiency and improved product mix.
PAT rose to ₹83 Cr with margins up ~240 bps, attributed to operating leverage, cost control and better business mix.
Treasury investments plus cash and cash equivalents stood at ₹195 Cr at FY26.
Working capital days improved to 55 in FY26 from 80 in FY25 on faster inventory turnover and better payable terms.
Sangam was recognised as a four-star export house.

guidance.statement: Aspire to double PAT again in FY27 from ₹83 Cr in FY26.
FY27 top line growth similar to FY26's 12.9%, with no abnormal growth as utilisation is high.
Renewable share of power to reach 70%+ in five quarters, adding ₹50-60 Cr annual EBITDA.

industry: Consumer Discretionary > Textiles > Textiles & Apparels > Other Textile Products

operating_notes.text: FY26 exports reached ₹1,167 Cr, described as an all-time high, from ₹1,109 Cr in FY25.
Q4FY26 capacity utilisation: Green Fibre 95%, PV Fabric 98%, Denim Fabric 49%, Garment 97%.
Recycled polyester fibre plant has 45 TPD (16,020 MT a year) capacity, meeting ~50% of daily polyester fibre requirement.
Order book is 50-70 days across segments; garment utilisation at about 49%.
About 50% of polyester fibre is in-house, targeted to rise to 75-80%; about 50% of denim raw material is in-house.
C9 brand contributes 40-45% of garment business; balance is contract manufacturing.
Captive renewable sources cater to 30% of total power requirement; expected to reach 70% in nine months.
Acquisition of RPSF unit in October 2025 expected to yield annual cost savings of ₹14-15 Cr.
Management plans ₹1,500 Cr capex over the next three financial years for renewables, cotton yarn expansion, and automation.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹883.92 Cr (+20.4% YoY), net profit ₹32.88 Cr (+245.4% YoY).
Q4 & FY26 investor presentation (22 Apr 2026): FY26 revenue ₹3,243 Cr (+12.9% YoY), EBITDA ₹329 Cr, PAT ₹83 Cr (+159.7% YoY); 12 MW hybrid renewable capacity commenced March 2026.
Sangam (India) Limited uploaded audio recording of its 23 April 2026 investor meet on its website.

Q4 & FY26 earnings call (23 Apr 2026): management aspires to double FY27 PAT again, sees ₹50-60 Cr annual EBITDA from renewables once 70%+ power share is reached in five quarters, and says new capex benefits will not come in FY27.
Sangam (India) Limited announced the dispatch of AGM notices and scheduled its 40th AGM for June 29, 2026, with the final dividend record date on June 22, 2026.
Shareholders approved Mr. Ranjan Jagetia’s (DIN: 11848375) appointment as Independent Director via postal ballot on October 15, 2026, with 40,664,411 votes in favor and 218 against.
India Ratings upgraded Sangam (India)'s long-term bank loan ratings to IND A (Stable) and assigned ratings to new ₹1,005 Cr facilities.
